addGuestsHandler constructs EventManager with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the mutation is allowed for attendees and team admins/owners. External calendar events are normally owned by the booking organizer/host, so using the requester's credentials can fail to update the correct calendar or update nothing. The handler loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Use the booking owner/host (or the credentials associated with the destination calendar) for the calendar update.

Dialog state is not consistently reset when closed

AddGuestsDialog resets `multiEmailValue` only on cancel or successful mutation, and does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on success. Closing via `onOpenChange` (for example, Escape or overlay click) leaves previous emails and validation errors in state, so reopening can show stale values or stale invalid-email warnings. Reset form state whenever the dialog closes or opens.

Error toast fallback is unreachable

In AddGuestsDialog, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` never uses the fallback. If `err.data?.code` or `err.message` is missing, users may see `undefined: ...` instead of a friendly message. Build the message conditionally.

Guests array is unbounded

The mutation schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length or minimum count. A client can submit an arbitrarily large number of emails, causing bulk attendee creation and mass email fan-out. Add a reasonable `.min(1).max(N)` and server-side uniqueness validation.

Hardcoded English tooltip in MultiEmail

The remove-email control uses `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`, which is not localized through `t()`. Users in non-English locales will see English text. Use a translation key.

No booking status check before adding guests

After loading the booking, addGuestsHandler only checks existence and permissions. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. The API can therefore add attendees to cancelled or past bookings, send notification emails, and attempt calendar updates for events that should no longer be modified. Add a status/eligibility check (for example, only upcoming accepted bookings unless intentionally broader).

No tests for new addGuests mutation

The PR introduces a privileged mutation with nontrivial permission checks, guest deduplication/case handling, blacklist filtering, calendar updates, and email selection, but no automated tests are included. Maintainers would want coverage for organizer/attendee/team admin permissions, cancelled bookings, duplicate/case-variant emails, blacklisted emails, and the email template selection.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count is incremented from a stale value

Both failure paths (lines 184 and 195) set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the SMS attempt. If two cron executions process the same reminder, or if the row is updated between the read and write, increments can be lost or applied incorrectly, preventing deletion after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment and guard the update for unscheduled reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry cleanup deletes WorkflowReminders of any method

The deleteMany query uses OR with a second condition that only checks retryCount > 1. This deletes every WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, not just unscheduled SMS reminders. Since retryCount is on the shared WorkflowReminder table, EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders or scheduled SMS rows that ever have retryCount > 1 can be deleted. Scope the retry cleanup to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and likely scheduled: false.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior

The PR introduces a retry counter and deletes reminders after repeated SMS scheduling failures, but no automated tests verify that retryCount is incremented on failure, that reminders are deleted only after the intended number of failures, and that non-SMS reminders are unaffected. This logic is prone to regressions.

Retry update in catch can abort the whole cron handler

The catch block awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update to increment retryCount. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted after the initial findMany or due to a DB error, the exception is not caught and will terminate the loop, leaving remaining reminders unprocessed. The same applies to the failure-path update. Use updateMany or wrap the retry increment in its own try/catch and ignore not-found errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Org scope excludes direct org members' individual bookings when there are no child teams

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches member user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. If an organization has no child teams, teamIds still contains the org ID and direct org memberships can exist, but the generated condition only matches team bookings (teamId = ANY([orgId]) AND isTeamBooking = true). Individual bookings of org members (isTeamBooking = false) are omitted. Memberships should be fetched for [orgId, ...childTeamIds] regardless of whether child teams exist.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

false_positives.candidate:
Authorization OR fragment can be returned without enclosing parentheses

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition may produce SQL shaped like (A) OR (B), but getBaseConditions returns authConditions unchanged when there is no filter condition. If a caller composes this fragment with additional predicates, for example WHERE ${baseConditions} AND another_condition, SQL precedence makes the added predicate apply only to the last OR branch, potentially returning rows outside the authorized set. The exposed condition should always be wrapped in parentheses, or the builders should return parenthesized fragments.

Member enumeration for raw authorization does not explicitly filter accepted memberships

isOrgOwnerOrAdmin checks membership.accepted, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition call MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without an accepted filter. If that repository method can return pending or invited memberships, their user IDs are included in the userId = ANY(...) condition and their individual bookings become visible in org/team insights. Add an explicit accepted filter or ensure the repository guarantees it.

No integration test executes the org/team ANY raw SQL paths

The only $queryRaw integration test uses user scope, which generates simple equality predicates. The org/team authorization conditions that use = ANY(${array}) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects and never run against the database. This leaves array parameter binding and the actual row-filtering behavior of the high-risk org/team scopes unverified. Add integration tests that execute org/team base conditions and assert included and excluded rows.

Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified ordering of repository results

The test expects exact arrays inside ANY(...) in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds without explicit ordering. If the database returns teams or memberships in a different order, the Prisma.sql values differ and the test fails even though the SQL is semantically the same. Sort IDs deterministically in the service or make the assertion order-independent.

Public findMany API removed without replacement or caller updates

The diff deletes findMany and changes the public condition methods from returning Prisma where-input objects to returning raw Prisma.Sql fragments. Any existing caller that used InsightsBookingService.findMany or composed the old where objects will break. Since no consumer files are updated in this PR, confirm the service is unused elsewhere or update callers or provide a compatibility adapter before merging.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Attempting to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt with an empty updateMany

SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is used to update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. An empty data object is fragile: depending on Prisma behavior it may be a no-op or may not reliably update @updatedAt for updateMany. If the intent is to touch records, pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sed -i '' is macOS/BSD-specific

The script uses sed -i '' -E, which fails on GNU/Linux because GNU sed treats '' as a backup suffix/file argument. If the script is intended to be cross-platform, use a portable in-place editing approach or detect the platform.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Authorization failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError

Throwing a plain Error for a missing or unauthorized credential produces a generic/internal tRPC error. Use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN so clients can distinguish authorization failures from unexpected server errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hardcoded en-US date format ignores user locale

The cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). This always renders US English formatting even when the user has another locale. Use the active app locale or the user's locale instead of hardcoding en-US.

false_positives.candidate:
Actions container renders even when dropdown is hidden

The wrapper always renders <div className="flex w-32 justify-end"> around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for a delegation credential with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, this still reserves layout space and may misalign cards/alerts. Render the actions container only when an action is actually visible.

Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the max updatedAt for all CalendarCache rows for a credential, without filtering expiresAt >= now(). Other cache-read paths ignore expired rows. This can make the UI display a cache status and delete action for expired/stale cache entries that would not actually be served.

Credential lookup fetches full credential row unnecessarily

prisma.credential.findFirst is called without a select, retrieving the entire credential record including encrypted secrets, only to check existence/ownership. Use select: { id: true } or select only the fields needed for authorization to avoid loading sensitive credential material into memory.

Delete cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars query

The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. It does not invalidate or refetch trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, which is the query supplying cacheUpdatedAt to this component. After a successful cache deletion, the UI can continue showing the old cache status until some other refetch happens. The disconnect mutation already invalidates related queries; deleteCache should do the same.

ENV_FILE relative path depends on current working directory

ENV_FILE="../.env" assumes the script is run from the scripts directory. If run from the repository root or another directory, it may create or modify the wrong .env file. Derive the path from the script location or use a repository-root-relative path.

No automated tests for deleteCache authorization or cache status aggregation

The PR introduces a destructive deleteCache mutation and a new cache-status aggregation method, but no unit/integration tests are included. Tests should cover at least: authorized deletion, rejection for another user's credential, correct getCacheStatusByCredentialIds behavior for multiple/expired cache rows, and connectedCalendars enrichment.

UserWithCalendars now requires additional selected-calendar fields

The exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars entries. This is a potentially breaking change for consumers of this exported/legacy type that construct or mock these objects, especially if they do not have these fields. If the fields are required by downstream code, this should be documented and call sites updated; otherwise consider keeping them optional.

connectedCalendars handler bypasses CalendarCache initialization/mock

The handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, while other cache read paths use CalendarCache.init(...), which can return a mock/no-op implementation when calendar-cache is disabled. If that gating is intentional, this handler can still expose DB-backed cache status even when calendar-cache functionality is disabled. Use the same factory or make the direct DB access intentional and documented.

deleteCache authorization only allows directly owned credentials

The handler checks credential ownership with { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }. Connected calendars can include delegation/team/service-account style credentials, and the UI explicitly handles delegationCredentialId. If a visible credential is not directly owned by the session user, the UI may show 'Delete cached data' but the mutation will fail. The authorization check should match the access model used to expose the credential, or the UI should hide the action when deletion is not permitted.

dev:cron uses npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency

The script uses 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not present in dependencies or devDependencies. npx may download tsx on demand, causing nondeterministic versions, network dependence, and failures in offline or restricted environments. Add tsx as a devDependency or use the already available ts-node.

updateManyByCredentialId accepts overly broad Prisma update type

The method types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which can include relational nested updates. prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany only supports scalar/mutation update fields. Use Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput or a narrower type to prevent invalid callers from compiling or failing at runtime.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget

The reminder cancellation loop calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting them. The request can finish before the database updates or external cancellations complete, which is especially risky in serverless environments; cancellations may be lost and reminders may still be sent.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete leaves the WorkflowReminder unchanged

deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch returns after the SendGrid request without updating or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Callers that do not cascade-delete the reminder (for example the reschedule path) leave a stale scheduled reminder, and if the external cancellation fails there is no state that can be retried or cleaned up by the cron job.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
A single failing SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all cancelled reminders

The cron cancellation loop awaits each SendGrid cancellation inside a single try/catch. If any reminder fails (null or invalid referenceId, SendGrid error, rate limit, etc.), control jumps to the catch and the remaining cancelled reminders are not canceled or deleted. Because the failing reminder remains in the table, subsequent runs can repeatedly stop at the same reminder, leaving other emails to be sent.

Cancel query does not filter by EMAIL or non-null referenceId

The query for reminders to cancel does not restrict to EMAIL reminders or require a non-null referenceId. If a SMS reminder or a reminder with a null referenceId ever has cancelled = true, the code will pass that referenceId to SendGrid, likely causing an error that aborts the cancellation loop.

Delayed cron cancellation leaves a race window where emails can still be sent

Cancellations are only processed by a cron job every 15 minutes. If a booking is canceled shortly after a cron run and a reminder is scheduled to send before the next run, the reminder will still be sent. This leaves a last-minute cancellation race even though the booking is canceled.

Paid booking cancellation skips workflow reminder cancellation

In the paid booking branch the handler returns before reaching the workflow reminder cancellation loop. Canceled/refunded paid bookings therefore do not cancel scheduled workflow emails or SMS, so reminders can still be sent.

Reschedule request does not await reminder cancellations

requestReschedule calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting them. The mutation can return before cancellations complete, so if the environment terminates work after the response or a call fails, old reminders may remain and be sent.

SMS cancellation has no fallback when Twilio cancel fails

deleteScheduledSMSReminder only deletes the reminder after a successful Twilio cancellation. If twilio.cancelSMS throws, the error is logged and the reminder remains scheduled, and there is no cancelled flag or cron retry for SMS. A transient Twilio failure can therefore cause SMS reminders for canceled or rescheduled bookings to be sent.

Workflow deletion does not await external reminder cancellations

When deleting a workflow, scheduled reminder cancellations are started in a forEach and not awaited before workflow.deleteMany runs. Cascade deletion can remove the reminder rows and the request can end before the SendGrid/Twilio cancellation completes; if the external cancel fails, scheduled messages for a deleted workflow may still be sent.

Workflow update ignores asynchronous reminder maintenance

The workflow update mutation starts asynchronous reminder cancellation and creation in map/forEach callbacks without awaiting them. The mutation can return before those operations finish, causing inconsistent reminder state, silent failures, and unhandled promise rejections.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One failing calendar import can reject all availability results

getCachedResults uses Promise.all over getCalendar calls. getCalendar now awaits dynamic app imports, so a rejected import or initialization error for one credential rejects the whole Promise.all and makes availability fail for all calendars. Consider Promise.allSettled or a per-credential catch that returns null/empty for the failing calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach is not awaited when deleting recurring calendar events

Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for async callbacks. In the recurring cancellation path, getCalendar and deleteEvent are awaited inside the callback, and only the resolved delete result is later pushed into apiDeletes. The later Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can therefore run before these operations are finished or before anything is pushed. External calendar deletions may not complete before the response, and rejections are unhandled. Use Promise.all(credentials.map(...)) and collect the deletion promises.

false_positives.candidate:
Video adapters are loaded sequentially

getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore dynamic import inside a for...of loop. When multiple credentials are supplied, module loading is serialized even though the imports are independent. Use Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...)) to load adapters in parallel.

Warning logs the module object instead of the app identifier

The warning interpolates paymentApp, which is the resolved module namespace or undefined, so it prints [object Module]/undefined rather than the missing app identifier. Log paymentAppCredentials.app?.dirName or appId to make the warning actionable. The same pattern exists in other payment-app lookups.

`await apiDeletes` does not wait for the queued integration deletions

apiDeletes is an array of promises/values, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself, not its elements. In the paid cancellation branch the handler continues immediately, so external calendar/video deletions are not awaited and any rejection becomes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` if these operations should be awaited.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end time uses slot start instead of slot end

In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` twice instead of using the slot end time or start time plus event length. As a result, a slot that starts before the working-hours end but extends past it passes the check, allowing bookings that run outside the configured availability.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects are compared with ===

The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two Dayjs object references, not their timestamps. This is never true for equal times. If a zero-length date override is used to represent an unavailable period or special case, this branch will not behave as intended. Use `.isSame()` instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Active date override filter compares wall-clock override start as a UTC instant

The override conversion treats `override.start` as a wall-clock time encoded in UTC, but activeOverrides filters by comparing `dayjs.utc(override.start)` directly against the invitee day's UTC interval. For large timezone offsets, this can exclude an override that belongs to the invitee date or include one that belongs to another date. For example, an override stored as 14:00Z for an invitee in UTC+14 may be filtered out because the invitee date spans roughly D-1 10:00Z to D 10:00Z, even though the converted local time is D 22:30.

Date override check skips busy-time validation

In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override loop, the function returns true immediately before executing the busy.every check. This means existing bookings or calendar busy times are ignored for slots covered by a date override, which can expose already-booked slots and allow double bookings.

Date override date comparison depends on server local timezone

The code formats `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` using the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is formatted as UTC. If the server timezone is not UTC, a converted date override near midnight can be assigned to the wrong calendar date, causing overrides to be matched or ignored incorrectly. The comparison should use UTC explicitly.

Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled incorrectly

The dateOverrides.find callback returns true when the slot is outside the particular override it is checking. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same date, a slot that is inside one override will be outside another override, causing find to return that other override and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. Valid slots can therefore be hidden whenever multiple date overrides exist for one day.

No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides

The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only checks timezone conversion for a personal event. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that only slots within the fixed host's date override are returned.

Timezone shift drops date changes when an override crosses midnight

After adding the timezone offset, the code extracts only `.hour()` and `.minute()` to build startTime and endTime. If the offset moves the override across midnight, the date change is discarded. The override can then be placed on the wrong invitee day or produce an end time earlier than the start time, causing missing or incorrect slots.

Working-hours validation rejects multi-interval schedules and can treat users with no hours as available

The workingHours.find logic returns true when the slot is outside a particular working-hours interval. If a user has multiple working intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval is outside another interval, so the slot is rejected. Conversely, if the user has no working-hours entry for that weekday, the function falls through to the busy check and may mark the user available even though they have no availability. The check should require the slot to be contained in at least one working-hours interval and reject when none matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsafe lookup of sender login can crash installation

GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') to integration.metadata['sender']['login'] using direct subscripting. If an existing Integration lacks metadata.sender, sender is not a dict, login is absent, or metadata is None (legacy rows, webhook payloads without sender, or integrations created before this change), this raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use defensive lookups and return error() when the sender identity is unavailable.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
Direct-install redirect can reverse with a None installation_id

If a request has setup_action=install and no pipeline but lacks installation_id, the code calls reverse('integration-installation', args=[provider_id, None]). Depending on the URL route converter this can generate an invalid URL or raise. Validate that installation_id is present before reversing, and otherwise redirect to a safe fallback.

OAuth authorize URL is built without URL-encoding parameters

The redirect to GitHub's authorize endpoint is built by interpolating client_id, state, and redirect_uri directly into a query string. redirect_uri contains characters such as ':' and '/' and should be percent-encoded per OAuth/form-urlencoded requirements. Use urllib.parse.urlencode to construct the URL; otherwise the request may be rejected by stricter OAuth servers/proxies, and future values with special characters could break the redirect.

Ownership check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist

The authenticated GitHub user is only checked when an active Integration row already exists. When Integration.DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() and build_integration will create the integration from the supplied installation_id without proving that the OAuth-authenticated user controls that installation. If a Sentry Integration record is absent because the webhook was delayed/failed or the data is legacy, a user who supplies a known installation_id could bind someone else's GitHub App installation to their organization. The flow should fail closed or verify ownership before advancing.

Token exchange and user fetch can 500 instead of showing the failure page

OAuthLoginView exchanges the OAuth code and fetches user info, but only parsing of the token response is wrapped in try/except. safe_urlopen and get_user_info can raise on network failures, timeouts, or non-successful GitHub responses. In those cases the request will return a 500 rather than the intended github-integration-failed error response. These calls should be guarded and return error() on failure.

installation_id is accepted and bound even during OAuth callback

OAuthLoginView binds installation_id from the query string on every dispatch, including OAuth callback requests, and does so before validating the state parameter. GitHub does not include installation_id in the OAuth redirect, so a crafted callback can alter the pipeline's stored installation_id, or mutate pipeline state even when state validation fails. Bind installation_id only during the initial step, after state validation, or avoid overwriting a value already bound in pipeline state.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import

The dataclass declares queued: datetime = timezone.now(), so the default is evaluated once when the module is imported rather than per instance. All AssignmentSource objects created via from_integration will carry the same process-start timestamp, making the field misleading and unsafe for any future freshness/TTL logic. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
to_dict() produces a non-JSON-safe Celery payload

to_dict returns asdict(self), leaving queued as a Python datetime. This dict is passed directly to Celery as task kwargs in sync_group_assignee_outbound. The payload is therefore not JSON-serializable and relies on pickle; if JSON serialization is used, apply_async will fail. Even when a custom encoder stringifies the datetime, from_dict does not parse it back. Serialize queued explicitly, for example as an ISO-8601 string, and deserialize it in from_dict.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalid assignment source silently disables cycle protection

When assignment_source_dict is present but AssignmentSource.from_dict cannot construct an object, parsed_assignment_source becomes None and the task proceeds as if no source were provided. That silently removes the cycle protection for malformed or version-skewed payloads. At minimum, record a log or metric for unparsable assignment_source_dict; ideally make the payload schema stable and validate required fields.

New Celery task kwarg is not backward compatible with old workers

The task signature adds assignment_source_dict, but old workers have a sync_assignee_outbound function that accepts only external_issue_id, user_id, and assign. In a mixed-version deploy, new producers can enqueue tasks with the new kwarg and old workers will raise TypeError, causing assignee sync failures and retries. This needs a backward-compatible task rollout or compatibility handling.

No test that deassignment with a matching AssignmentSource is suppressed

The added test covers suppression for GroupAssignee.objects.assign with a matching AssignmentSource, but there is no analogous test for GroupAssignee.objects.deassign with a matching AssignmentSource. Since deassignment also triggers sync_group_assignee_outbound, a regression in the deassign path could reintroduce sync cycles without being caught.

Tasks are still enqueued for the integration that triggered the change

sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues a task for every linked external issue, including issues belonging to the integration identified by assignment_source. Each of those tasks loads ExternalIssue, Organization, Integration, and installation only to exit because should_sync returns False. For frequent inbound assignment webhooks this creates avoidable Celery tasks and database/service lookups; filtering out the source integration before enqueuing would be cheaper.

false_positives.candidate:
Occurrences are produced before detector state is committed

process_detectors calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for each evaluation result before handler.commit_state_updates is called. If the process crashes or the state commit fails after the Kafka produce call, the dedupe/state used to prevent reprocessing is not persisted. A retry or reprocessing of the same data packet can then pass the dedupe check again and emit duplicate occurrences or status changes.

A valid StatefulDetectorHandler subclass with counter_names == [] will therefore crash during evaluation. true_positives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

true_positives.golden_comment: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
added sleep in test is disabled by monkeypatch

test_basic monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op, then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time to observe the changed drift. Because the monkeypatch is active, this call does not actually wait, so the test remains timing-dependent and may be racy.
